counterfactual_missing_items: No histopathologic or biopsy confirmation is provided to prove an invasive subtype
No diffuse erythema, edema, or peau d'orange is described, making inflammatory breast cancer unsupported
No nipple-areolar eczematous change is described, making Paget disease unsupported
decisive_items: Chest CT demonstrated a right breast mass suggestive of malignancy
response.rationale: R5 is the best match because it integrates the right breast mass, malignant imaging features, skin ulceration, and the invasive/complicated clinical picture. R3 is the closest runner-up but is merely a less specific breast cancer label. R2 requires diffuse inflammatory skin findings, absent here; R1 requires nipple-areolar involvement, absent here; R6 falsely infers a triple-negative subtype from normal serum markers; C1 only restates laterality without the substructure or malignant imaging evidence.

rejected.why: Skin ulceration alone does not establish inflammatory breast cancer; no diffuse erythema, edema, or peau d'orange is present.
Paget disease would involve the nipple-areolar complex, but the ulcerated mass is described in the breast at 2.5 cm from the nipple without nipple eczematous changes.
Normal serum tumor markers cannot by themselves establish triple-negative breast cancer; receptor status and pathology are absent.
This only adds laterality to a breast cancer label and lacks the invasive subtype and radiological support seen in R5.
